_meta.note: Industry, peers, street (notes standing on 30-Sep-2026), ownership (Jun-2026 categories; named holders from the latest public list, 31-Mar-2026), governance, moat, critiques, gaps, conflicts.

industry.gst: GST 2.0 (22-Sep-2025) cut tax on small cars; industry rebounded 17% in H2FY26 (management).
industry.luxury: JLR: China luxury tax from mid-Jul-2025 and weak demand (China wholesales -27% in FY26, -25% in Q1FY27); US tariffs on UK cars 27.5% until the UK-US deal cut them to 10% within a quota (incremental tariff cost ~GBP525m in FY26); Middle East (6% of sales) hit by the Iran conflict in Q1FY27; VME (discounts) 7.1% of revenue in Q1FY27 vs 4.1%.

competition.india: Tata is #2 on Vahan registrations (14.3% in Q1FY27, +200bp) behind Maruti Suzuki and ahead of Mahindra and Hyundai; ~40-43% of India's electric car market (competition rising: MG, Mahindra, Hyundai, Maruti e-Vitara).
competition.jlr: Competes with BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Porsche, Audi, Lexus and Chinese premium brands; Range Rover, Range Rover Sport and Defender were 81% of Q1FY27 wholesales; Jaguar is being relaunched as an electric-only brand (Type 01 from early 2027).

excluded.BAJAJ-AUTO: Earnings distorted: the Mar-2026 quarter carries ~Rs1,894 cr of other income when Bajaj took control of KTM, which is consolidated from then, so its trailing P/E on 30-Sep-2026 sits on an inflated TTM EPS (same exclusion as the Eicher Motors report).
excluded.ESCORTS: Earnings distorted: a Rs1,085 cr exceptional gain on selling the railway business (Jun-2025 quarter) depresses its trailing P/E, and the remaining company is not the one in its five-year median (same exclusion as the Eicher Motors report).

notes.HYUNDAI: Listed Oct-2024: no five-year history, so not in the de-rating median; shown in the peer table.
notes.MARUTI: Closest listed pure-play Indian car maker: the proxy for the India PV multiple.
notes.TMCV: The demerged commercial-vehicle company listed Nov-2025; no history, not used.

governance.board: Chaired by N Chandrasekaran (Tata Sons). After the demerger the board was rebuilt: MD & CEO Shailesh Chandra (Oct-2025), JLR CEO P B Balaji as non-executive director, five independent directors after Om Prakash Bhatt retired (Mar-2026). Auditor B S R & Co. LLP. Promoters (Tata Sons and group companies) 42.5%, no pledge disclosed.
governance.relatedParty: JLR has a long-term battery supply agreement with Agratas (Tata Sons' battery company) for its UK gigafactory; shareholder approval sought for the related-party transactions (AR FY26 AGM notice).
